root_cause: On a group-subscription effect restart the new run overwrote groupLifecycleRef, so nothing referenced the retired run's still-running setup; the retired setup tracked its whenIdle/drain only when it finished, after a stale-Welcome replace may already have snapshotted pendingDrainRef, so the replace could destroy/rejoin under the old ingest's state save.
fix: New trackRetiredSetup(pending, groupId, setup, handedOver) in replaceTeardown.ts: one pendingDrainRef entry that settles after the setup and then all work it handed over. The effect keeps a per-run runSetups list (setupDone + handedOver array filled by retireDispatcher and the aborted-after-subscribe path) and registers each in its cleanup, synchronously with the abort.

tests_added.kinds: real trackRetiredSetup + teardownForReplace: late handed-over idle blocks a replace until settled; never-settling handover/setup fails closed; rejections count as settled; entry dropped when nothing handed over; handedOver read lazily after the setup settled. Gap (accepted, no-jsdom convention): the MarmotContext cleanup wiring itself has no unit test.

e2e.result: non-relay 72 passed; relay 353 passed, 19 skipped, 0 failed; no INVALID marker.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The fix lives in a React effect the project cannot unit-test (no jsdom), so correctness rests on two orderings (pushes before finishSetup; registration synchronous with abort) that only review verifies.
retrospective.surprised_by: Reviewing the drain set showed more untracked work started from inside the subscription (onMembersChanged commit, profile send); filed separately as replace-does-not-await-onmemberschanged.
